hints: Resolve forces vertically: the vertical forces in equilibrium give $3P\sin 55^\circ = 20$.
Solve this single-variable equation directly for $P$: $P = \frac{20}{3\sin 55^\circ}$.
Resolve forces horizontally to relate $P$ and $\theta$: $3P\cos 55^\circ = 2P\cos\theta$.
Divide both sides by $P$ to get $\cos\theta = 1.5\cos 55^\circ$, and take $\arccos$ to find $\theta$ to 1 decimal place.
walkthrough:
State the conditions for coplanar equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \Sigma F_x = 0$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation (taking upwards as positive):
$$3P\sin 55^\circ - 20 = 0 \implies 3P\sin 55^\circ = 20$$

Divide both sides by $3\sin 55^\circ$ to isolate $P$:
$$P = \frac{20}{3\sin 55^\circ}$$

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation (taking rightwards as positive):
$$2P\cos\theta - 3P\cos 55^\circ = 0 \implies 2P\cos\theta = 3P\cos 55^\circ$$

Divide both sides by the common factor $P$:
$$2\cos\theta = 3\cos 55^\circ$$

Divide both sides by $2$ to isolate $\cos\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{3}{2}\cos 55^\circ = 1.5\cos 55^\circ$$

Take the inverse cosine to determine the acute angle $\theta$:
$$\theta = \arccos(0.860365) \approx 30.643^\circ = 30.6^\circ \text{ (to 1 d.p.)}$$
